note: The provider and model catalog the settings dialog populates from. A STARTING POINT, NOT A REGISTRY: model identifiers change, are retired, and are added far faster than this file is edited, so treat a missing model as this file being out of date rather than as the model not existing. Nothing here is probed or verified. The engine never calls a provider to build this list, and cannot be made to: rolePing is the only path that verifies a model or a key, and it is spend-touching and fires only when a user asks for it by hand. Model IDs verified against provider announcements 2026-08-17 by web search; they will drift again.
maintenance: Owned by the repository owner and corrected through ordinary commits, so a wrong or missing model identifier is a one-line edit rather than a code change. Adding a provider means adding an entry here AND to the closed enum the engine validates against; the engine derives that enum from this file, so the two cannot drift.

fields.id: The value stored in a role's `provider`. The VENDOR name, not a display name.
fields.label: For rendering only. A client shows this; it never sends it.
fields.endpointDefault: Offered when a role picks this provider. A role may override it.
fields.keyRequired: false only where the endpoint is local and no credential exists to point at.
fields.models[].reasoningEffort: The accepted values, or NULL where the model has no such control. Null is the only encoding of unsupported: a string like 'none' would read as a supported setting deliberately turned off, which is a different claim.
fields.models[].note: Optional. Present where a model's reasoning control does not work the way the field name suggests.

providers.label: Ollama (local)
providers.note: THESE ARE SUGGESTIONS, NOT AN INVENTORY. Every other provider's list is unknowable without a paid call, so a static list is the only honest option there. Ollama is different: what is actually installed is local truth, reported by `ollama list` and by /api/tags, and this list will happily name models the owner does not have. Reading the installed set would be zero-spend and correct, and it is deliberately NOT done here because providerCatalog is specified as a static unprobeable table. If a client shows this list to pick a local model, say that it is a suggestion.
